newsitem.title: USA: IBM jumps again ahead of earnings report.
newsitem.headline: IBM jumps again ahead of earnings report.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. stock surged again Tuesday in advance of the computer giant's fourth-quarter earnings report, slated to be issued after the stock market closes.
IBM, in a break with tradition, is releasing its results after the stock market close rather than before the market opens.
The Armonk, N.Y.-based company is expected to report solid profits for the quarter but analysts expect the stronger dollar in Europe and Japan will hurt earnings.
IBM stock rose $2.25 to $169.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. On Monday, the stock closed up $1.75 at $167 in active trading.

Analysts said there was no particular negative significance in IBM's reporting after the close. The company is trying to avoid the drastic swings in its stock price that have occurred during its analysts' conference call, which IBM hosts after the earnings are released.
Traders and analysts also said they were not hearing any so-called "whisper" numbers ahead of its earnings report.
"The whisper circuit has been pretty quiet here," said Bill Milton, an analyst at brokerage Brown Brothers Harriman. "The whisper circuit was very active for Intel last week."
"Whisper" numbers refer to estimates traders and analysts are "whispering about," which are different than published Wall Street estimates.

The consensus industy analysts' estimate for IBM's fourth quarter earnings is $3.88 a share, with estimates ranging from $3.13 to $4.32 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst estimates. The estimates include restructuring costs for employee buyouts, which are no longer counted as a charge.
In 1995's fourth quarter, IBM earned $1.7 billion, or $3.09 per share, including special charges.
The impact of the stronger dollar is expected to hurt earnings by 10 cents a share to 35 cents a share, analysts have said.
"I think it was a solid quarter," Milton said of IBM. "Solid is unspectacular."
